advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either lower PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to match the documented ~10 s refusal, or change the docs/docstring to state the real worst-case bound.
evidence: scripts/check_verify_host.py: `#: Per-probe wall-clock bound. Both network probes finish in about 2 s on a capable host.`
docs/local-dev-env.md (added): "which refuses in about 10 seconds on a host that lacks a capability the suite needs"
Two network probes (package_index_probe, semgrep_validate_probe) each use timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, so the worst case is 2 x 300 s.
advisory.finding: The docs and module docstring say the preflight refuses "in about 10 seconds", but each network probe is only bounded by a 300 s timeout. A sandbox that drops outbound traffic silently, instead of refusing it, can make `make verify` hang for up to ~10 minutes before refusing.
scenarios: An egress filter that drops packets: pip retries until it gives up, and semgrep --validate waits on its rule-lint download, each up to 300 s.

dropped.finding: No test covers unix_socket_probe when creating the socket itself is denied. Only a denied bind() is tested. `server = socket_factory(...)` sits outside the try/except OSError, so a factory that raises PermissionError on construction never returns (False, detail) from the probe. The exception escapes to main's generic `probe raised ...` handler, and no test pins that this denial still produces a 'missing AF_UNIX' line.
merged_from: test_verify_runs_the_preflight_strictly_before_its_gates is a change-detector on the Makefile's text. It regex-parses the verify rule and asserts the exact recipe line `@$(MAKE) --no-print-directory lint typecheck import-convention test`, so behavior-preserving edits break it. Examples: adding a MAKEFLAGS passthrough, using `+$(MAKE)`, reflowing the line, or placing a non-`@#` comment. And it never checks what it claims to check: that make actually runs verify-host before the gates under -j/-k.
scenarios: A sandbox that blocks socket(AF_UNIX) creation, not bind. The probe's own contract (return False plus detail) is skipped, and correct reporting depends on main's catch-all. Nothing gates that.
dropped.suggested_fix: Move the server construction inside the try (or wrap it) so a construction OSError returns (False, detail). Then add a test with a factory whose __init__ raises PermissionError, asserting `ok is False` and 'PermissionError' in detail.
